task.instruction: Write a 180–220 word supervisor memo with the exact headings Observed, Next shift, and Checkpoint. Choose exactly one ten-rescan protocol for 90 minutes: the supervisor-assigned calibration sequence or the apprentice-selected sequence with oral rationale. Keep Box 4 local-only, preserve the date as circa 1908, and define a measurable checkpoint. Cite evidence IDs.

evidence.content: Twenty-four scans were completed; 22 are sharp and two crop the page margin.
Six scans omit the required color target.
The envelope says c. 1908; metadata currently says 1908.
Box 4 contains unredacted phone numbers and must not be uploaded outside the local workspace.

The next shift is 90 minutes and permits exactly ten rescans. The training register accepts one indivisible protocol: a supervisor-assigned calibration sequence or an apprentice-selected sequence with oral rationale; mixing protocols invalidates the checkpoint.
The apprentice reports confidence in scan order but uncertainty about color calibration.
A print apprentice completed 18 proofs; six missed the gray target, and one 45-minute block allowed either an eight-sheet calibration ladder or a self-selected correction set.
An audio trainee completed 20 transfers; three clipped peaks, and one 60-minute block allowed either a fixed gain drill or a trainee-chosen sequence with explanation.
